lesson.title: Two Misses. One Clue.
lesson.hook: You change your swing after every miss, while the same contact problem stays.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time your forehand feels rushed, notice whether the ball repeatedly crowds your hitting side at contact.

pro.label: Agassi's spacing
pro.moment: Coach Andy Zodin points to Agassi's non-hitting arm, extended across the body as he lines up the forehand: it creates "a distance between your body and the ball" for a consistent contact point.
pro.read: Notice the space before you change the swing.

drill.name: Space check
drill.how: Rally 20 forehands. After each, call "crowded", "good" or "reaching". Fix it with your feet, never the swing.

steps.name: The miss into the net
steps.sit: Your forehand goes into the net. Watch it again, held at the moment you hit it.
steps.q: What do you change on the next ball?
steps.payoff: The frame showed the ball jammed against your body. Space fixed it.
steps.principle: Check the space at contact before changing your swing.
steps.why: Held at contact, the ball is right beside your hip and your elbow is folded. Swinging differently can't fix that; a couple of small steps can.
steps.take: Missed? Before fixing the swing, check the space at contact.

lines.A: More space, the arm extends — deep, rally on.
lines.B: Still jammed — it comes off short, and they step in.
lines.C: Still jammed — faster just puts it in the net again.
lines.D: Still jammed — it lands short, and they step in.

steps.name: The long miss
steps.sit: This forehand goes long. Held at contact, there's plenty of space.
steps.q: What do you change this time?
steps.payoff: The frame ruled out spacing, so the target was the problem.
steps.principle: The clue also tells you what not to change.
steps.why: Held at contact, the arm is extended and the space is good. The miss came from aiming at the line, so a bigger target fixes it; more space changes nothing.
steps.take: Space looks fine? Then don't change it — look at the target.

lines.A: The space was already fine — same target, same miss: long.
lines.B: Inside the line, it lands deep — rally on.
lines.C: Harder at the line — long again.
lines.D: The grip wasn't it — the target still asks too much: long.

steps.name: The short miss
steps.sit: A different ball, a different miss: this one lands short. Held at contact again.
steps.q: What do you change on the next ball?
steps.payoff: A different miss, the same jammed contact, and the same fix.
steps.principle: Different misses can share one cause you can see.
steps.why: Last time it went into the net; now it's short. Held at contact, the ball is jammed against your body both times. Fix the space before the swing.
steps.take: Net one day, short the next? Check the space at contact first.

lines.A: Still jammed — it comes off short again.
lines.B: Still jammed — higher, but short again.
lines.C: More space, the arm extends — deep, rally on.
lines.D: Still jammed — a shorter swing and it flies long.
